topics.topic: Number and identity of tables owned by data_provider
questions: Does `data_provider` own two tables or the three subsequently named tables `ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`, `SERVICE_RIGHTS` and `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`?
Does `data_provider` own three tables as the three named constants and row models say, or only two tables as the opening clause says; if only two, which service data is combined or omitted?
Does `data_provider` own and import models for three tables, or must one of the three listed constants be removed or merged so that there are exactly two?

quotes: `models`, for exactly the row models and enumerations of its two tables:

`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`. Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementation emits only two tables by merging or omitting one service-data table, while another emits all three explicitly named tables; the release builder and service_access observe the difference.
judgement.why: The opening clause says there are exactly two tables, but the same passage explicitly specifies three distinct table constants and three row models.

bases.passage: `models`, for exactly the row models and enumerations of its two tables:

`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`. Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.

topics.topic: Applicable listener-host topology policy and scope of topology validation
questions: Does the configured-host policy follow the cited R0-19 same-host restriction, which the supplied State 0 text says was replaced, or the current R0-28, R0-29, R0-39 and Network surface topology that permits the VPS through WireGuard and the owner through the VPN; and must Registry validate any topology beyond IP-address syntax?

quotes: ### R0-28 — One production Registry on the owner's home server (owner, 2026-10-27; replaces R0-19's topology)

Client Portal on the VPS reaches the production Registry over a WireGuard
tunnel that the home server initiates; the home server publishes no listening
port to the internet for it. The tunnel carries the service API only, with
Portal's service token as on any other request (R0-27).

The addresses are the deployment's, as R0-19 says
   — the host's loopback where Registry runs on the host, its internal
   network where it runs in a container — so the configuration names them
   (owner, 2026-11-11, replacing the release-fixed addresses of 2026-11-01:
   one release cannot hold both).

The owner's deployment definition enforces this — `--host 127.0.0.1`
locally, a compose service with no published port on the VPS — and the owner
checks it when deploying; no component detects an exposure, and Registry
starts and answers as usual either way.
judgement.why: R0-28 expressly replaces R0-19's topology, R0-39 permits the protected cross-host WireGuard channel, and topology enforcement remains the owner's deployment responsibility rather than a Registry validation beyond the stated address checks.

topics.topic: Behavior when the service API address is present but all service tokens are absent
questions: When the four service tokens are absent but the service API address is present, must configuration reject the partial five-item group or start owner-only because no token was given?

quotes:
The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start: the service tokens and the
   service API's address all five or none — none makes an owner-only start,
   and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order;
judgement.why: A service API address with all four tokens absent is a partial five-item group and therefore fails on the first missing token.

topics.topic: Integrity rules and mismatch handling for SERVICE_RIGHTS and SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES
questions: After splitting this fact into `SERVICE_RIGHTS` and `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`, who guarantees that both tables contain exactly the same services, that every service has exactly one highest class, and that right rows are unique, and what happens if they disagree?

quotes:
A09 rule 2's table of the services, their
operations, and each service's highest class;

`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`. Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.

A09: telling a service by its token — the presented token compared in
constant time with each configured one, an unknown token refused like a wrong
one, without a limit (A17 rule 7) — and the service's operations and highest
class from the release (A09 rules 1, 2, 3);
judgement.why: No admissible history is shown in which a conforming release can omit, duplicate, or mismatch rows, because data_provider is required to embody A09 rule 2's fixed service table; the reviews would need a textual path that permits malformed release constants.

topics.topic: Module that owns environment-variable name constants
questions: Are environment-variable names owned solely by `runtime_settings`, or are they constants of `data_provider` under the rule that every generated-code value which is not an environment setting, enumeration member or model field type has `data_provider` as its one home?

topics.topic: Validated address representation and ownership of shared address parsing
questions: Does `load_configuration` return each validated address as raw text or as a parsed host-and-port value, and which module owns the one parsing used both for validation and for opening the listener?
